write_authority.note: One write authority for StrategySpec content, immutable versions, RegistryEntry identities and artifact-state. No independent full-spec/revision copy exists in the mounted app; the parallel authority referenced in architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §2/§5 (command_contract.py + pg_store.py from the superseded REGISTRY-STRATEGY-DURABILITY-PREREQUISITE-001 worktree) was never merged to dev and is not part of the retirement inventory below because it was never mounted. storage.build_registry_store no longer defaults an entirely unset REGISTRY_STORE_BACKEND to the in-memory store in any posture (generation-9 fix, reviewer finding 7) — it always requires an explicit memory or postgres selection; services/registry/conftest.py sets memory explicitly for this whole package's unit-test run.

capabilities.legal_transition: a new version for a strategy_id that already has registered StrategySpec entries must be either an idempotent replay of an existing (strategy_id, version) at the *same* registry_id, or declare explicit caller parent identity (lineage.parent_registry_ids naming an existing StrategySpec entry for that strategy_id; content checksum alone is not revision CAS and cannot adopt an intervening revision) AND be a strictly greater version than that parent's (no downgrade); if base_checksum is declared, it must match the expected parent entry's checksum. An arbitrary/out-of-sequence version, a downgrade below a linked parent's version, an omitted parent binding on a noninitial revision (400), a mismatched base_checksum against the parent entry (409), a stale parent whose version is not the current latest (409), or a *different* registry_id claiming an already-registered (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) is rejected (400/409). The identical atomic revision invariants apply to every StrategySpec representation (both inline metadata.strategy_spec and storage_ref references) on both typed POST /api/registry/strategy-specs and generic POST /api/registry/entries (both keyed and unkeyed) under the per-strategy advisory lock, while preserving distinct artifacts and name-only drafts. The (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) tuple is enforced as a real atomic unique identity at the store layer (register_if_absent's unique_fields, backed by PostgresJsonOwnerStore.insert_if_absent's table lock / RegistryStore's single process lock) — two different caller-supplied registry_ids racing the same tuple commit exactly one winner.
capabilities.status: implemented; real version/parent-linkage and base_checksum validation enforced atomically under per-strategy advisory lock across both typed and generic routes for all StrategySpec representations; omitted parent binding rejected with 400 (content checksum alone is not revision CAS), mismatched base_checksum and stale parent rejected with 409 Conflict

capabilities.legal_transition: governed artifact_state transition per ALLOWED_ARTIFACT_TRANSITIONS in models.py; CAS-guarded (RegistryConflictError/409 on a stale base — a caller-claimed expected_artifact_state/expected_version/expected_updated_at that does not match the durable row now fails the same CAS the same way a stale server-read snapshot would, instead of the caller's stale belief being silently discarded)
capabilities.durable_receipt: registry.command_receipts row when command_key is supplied, keyed by tenant+actor+registry_id+command_type('advance')+command_key (the command_type tag was added by the 2026-09-06 generation-9 pass so a metadata-CAS call and an advance sharing the same client-chosen command_key/registry_id/tenant/actor can never land on the same receipt row) and committed in the same Postgres transaction as the entry's artifact_state mutation (PostgresRegistryStore.commit_artifact_state_cas) — not a separate outbox; see services/registry/contract.md 'Command-receipt durability mechanism'. A replay returns the entry snapshot exactly as originally committed under that key and never re-runs the transition-legality/lineage business-rule check (which would otherwise spuriously reject a legitimate replay against the entry's already-post-transition current state).

bff_adapter_semantics.prior_defect: StrategyCommandAdapter._execute_strategy_action fabricated a resulting_status from a static action->status map and returned an authoritative_readback with zero owner I/O — architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §2. A later fix added real owner I/O but still (a) silently replaced the caller's expected_metadata CAS precondition with a freshly-fetched GET, defeating CAS, (b) discarded the real PATCH response in favor of a second, independent GET that could return stale/unrelated/empty data and still be reported as success, (c) never validated that the caller-supplied registry_id actually belonged to the requested strategy_id (a cross-strategy write could be reported as success for the wrong aggregate), (d) mislabeled a bare updated_at timestamp as "version" in the receipt, and (e) compared a genuine idempotent replay's PATCH response against an independent "current" owner GET, which spuriously failed (READBACK_MISMATCH) whenever a later, unrelated command had since moved the row on. A follow-up generation-9 review (2026-09-06) found the corrected non-replay readback comparison still (f) never verified the readback's own strategy_id/owner_tenant/version identity (a readback for a wholly different aggregate that happened to share the PATCH response's checksum/updated_at/metadata passed every check) and (g) never verified that the *requested* metadata was actually applied (an owner that silently no-op'd the write, returning old metadata in both the PATCH response and the readback, also passed every check); and the replay path (h) trusted a replay's self-reported metadata/last_actor/updated_at with no check beyond registry_id/checksum/version/owner_tenant identity — fields that never change on a metadata-only commit in the first place, so a forged replay reporting unrelated metadata, no actor, and a null commit time still passed.
bff_adapter_semantics.fix: update_params now requires and forwards the caller's own expected_metadata unchanged (no silent refresh-to-latest), authenticates callers strictly via services.runtime_auth_inbound.validate_request_auth enforcing strict JWT validation regardless of inherited permissive mode and requiring non-empty sub/tenant/roles/exp before any owner I/O (rejecting non-JWT/unscoped tokens with zero owner I/O), performs a real HTTP PATCH against the Registry metadata-CAS route without false commit-timestamp equality rejection, and independently reloads and validates the durable scoped receipt (command_key, registry_id, receipt_key, request_digest, committed_at, last_actor) from GET /api/registry/entries/{registry_id}/receipts/{command_key}. In both normal and idempotent-replay outcomes, the adapter validates the authoritative owner receipt rather than fabricating receipts from entry-only bodies. If an ambiguous transport exception (such as RemoteDisconnected) occurs during PATCH, the adapter attempts scoped receipt readback recovery without issuing a second mutation; if unconfirmed, it fails closed with retryable 503 UNCONFIRMED_COMMAND_RECEIPT. Both the PATCH response and any receipt are checked against the requested strategy_id, failing closed with STRATEGY_ID_MISMATCH on a cross-aggregate registry_id. The receipt's "version" field reports the entry's actual semver version. submit_review/promote_paper/activate/pause/archive still raise ActionUnavailableError naming the exact owner from command_contract.py.
bff_adapter_semantics.unrelated_scope_preserved: RankingFormula and Ranking action handling in the same adapter file is untouched by this task; their pre-existing fake-receipt pattern is not claimed solved here.

create_if_absent_replay_semantics.note: Both the StrategySpec facade's (POST /api/registry/strategy-specs) and the StrategyArtifact facade's (POST /api/registry/strategy-artifacts) same-registry_id create-if-absent replay path previously (a) returned the collision unconditionally with no tenant authorization on the existing row (generation-9 finding 1 — a different tenant's identical POST could read another tenant's private entry), and (b) compared the caller's replay payload against the row's *current* (possibly since-advanced/metadata-edited) fields rather than its original creation content (generation-9 finding 5 — a legitimate replay of the exact original request could be wrongly rejected as 'different content' once metadata had legitimately drifted under a separate, unrelated update_metadata call). Both facades now (a) authorize the existing row's owner_tenant (read-scoped, so a builtin's own idempotent bootstrap re-registration is unaffected — builtins are already publicly readable) before comparing/returning it, and (b) compare against RegistryService.get_creation_receipt's immutable original-creation snapshot when one was recorded, falling back to the live row for a legacy pre-fix entry. The row *returned* to the HTTP caller is always the live current view, never reverted — a replayed create is not a request to undo real progress (e.g. an already-granted approval).

generic_route_strategy_spec_serialized_c.note: POST /api/registry/entries previously ran the StrategySpec version/lineage invariant check (_validate_strategy_spec_version_lineage) as a separate, unlocked pre-check and then called the plain register() path — the same TOCTOU race the dedicated facade closed in an earlier pass (per-strategy_id Postgres advisory transaction lock, re-validating against the true latest-committed state) was left open on this route (generation-9 finding 2). register_entry now routes a full StrategySpec (an embedded metadata.strategy_spec, not a bare checksum reference) through RegistryService.register_strategy_spec_revision under the same lock whenever the artifact_type is strategy_spec.

readiness_owner_dependency_receipts_tabl.note: The Postgres readiness probe (main.py::_registry_owner_dependency) previously queried only the entries table, so a missing/dropped command_receipts table (required by every idempotency-keyed create/metadata/advance commit) reported ready=true while the next such commit would raise a 500 (generation-9 finding 8). The probe now also queries the configured receipts table.

tenant_scoped_aggregate_reads.note: GET /api/registry/strategies/{strategy_id}/latest-approved and GET /api/registry/strategies/{strategy_id}/deployment-view previously authenticated the caller but resolved the semver-latest approved entry across *all* tenants, so a caller in tenant B could receive tenant A's approved entry/deployment stage for a shared strategy_id. RegistryService.resolve_latest_approved/resolve_deployment_view (split_api.py) now accept an optional `visible` entry predicate; the two routes pass `_can_read_entry(ctx, entry)` so resolution itself is scoped to entries the caller's verified tenant (or an admin role, or a builtin) may see. The same `_can_read_entry` scoping was applied to the existing-versions lookup POST /api/registry/strategy-specs uses to decide the next legal semver (_validate_strategy_spec_version_lineage), which previously computed 'the latest known version' across all tenants for the same strategy_id.

generic_route_typed_content_validation.note: POST /api/registry/entries previously stored a caller-supplied checksum verbatim with no content validation, and only enforced lineage/sequence validation if inline metadata.strategy_spec was present. It now enforces the identical atomic revision sequencing invariants, parent lineage, and base checksum CAS for all StrategySpec representations (both inline metadata.strategy_spec and storage_ref/object_store references) under the per-strategy advisory lock, preventing noninitial reference revisions from bypassing caller base validation while preserving distinct artifacts and name-only drafts. In addition, inline strategy_spec payloads are schema-validated and their checksum is verified against the embedded content. Draft classification is strictly derived server-side from request structure, reserved draft_kind metadata markers on typed submissions and StrategySpec submissions are rejected (400), and mixing name with typed fields is rejected (400).

atomic_composite_identity_on_plain_creat.note: register() (the non-register_if_absent create path used by e.g. model_artifact entries and name-only drafts) previously inserted unconditionally with no composite-identity reservation at the store layer at all — only a non-atomic, best-effort application-layer check. RegistryStore.create/PostgresRegistryStore.create now accept unique_fields and atomically reserve (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) the same way register_if_absent does; a genuine collision under this path raises RegistryUniqueViolationError -> RegistryConflictError (409) instead of relying solely on the non-atomic pre-check.

idempotent_creation.note: POST /api/registry/entries had no idempotency concept: the name-only draft branch synthesized a fresh random strategy_id on every call, so a caller could not safely retry a dropped response without creating a second, divergent draft. An optional Idempotency-Key header now scopes creation through RegistryService.register_with_idempotency, backed by a new create_with_receipt on both storage backends (mirroring commit_metadata_cas's atomic reservation-then-commit pattern on Postgres, sharing one transaction with the entry insert). A replay under the same tenant/actor-scoped key returns the originally-created entry; the identity-generating factory is only invoked on a genuine first request. This is scoped to the generic entries route in this pass; register_strategy_spec/register_strategy_artifact/register_allocation_policy_artifact already have content-addressed idempotency via register_if_absent's composite-key replay match.

readiness_owner_dependency.note: services/registry/main.py registered /healthz//livez//readyz with no dependency check at all, so /readyz always returned 200/ready=true/dependencies={} regardless of whether the selected owner backend was actually reachable, including when backend selection silently resolved to the in-memory test double. main.py now registers a `registry_owner` dependency that performs a genuine short-lived Postgres connection probe (SELECT 1) on the durable backend, or explicitly reports `degraded`/`backend: memory` when the in-memory test double is selected, on every readiness check.
readiness_owner_dependency.remaining_gap: Not proven against a live Postgres outage/partition in this pass; the connection probe itself is genuine (fresh connect + SELECT 1, not a cached pool), but no test kills the database mid-run to observe the transition to error status.

auth_wiring_status.note: architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §3.3 requires reusing services/runtime_auth_inbound.py validate_request_auth with strict mode across Registry mutation routes. The 2026-09-06 corrective pass wires _authenticate_registry_write into every mutating route in service.py (register_entry, register_strategy_spec, register_strategy_artifact, register_allocation_policy_artifact, every advance route, mutate_strategy_artifact_entry, update_deployment_summary) — not just the metadata-CAS route — and additionally rejects a signature-valid JWT missing subject/tenant/role/expiry claims via _require_verified_identity. docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.control.yml already set PANTHEON_REGISTRY_AUTH_MODE=strict and REGISTRY_STORE_BACKEND=postgres for the registry service. A follow-up gen-5 pass additionally scopes register_strategy_spec's replay-return path (and the cross-tenant aggregate reads named above) through _authorize_write/_can_read_entry, since authentication alone does not scope which tenant's data a verified caller may read back.
